author: u. m. simon
title: Hawai'i Rainbow Wahine softball team falls to No. 10 UCLA after early lead - Maui Reporter
text:
The University of Hawai’i softball team lost 9-5 to No. 10 UCLA at Easton Stadium on April 2, despite taking an early lead and fighting until the final out. The Rainbow Wahine led through the first two innings and threatened in the seventh, but a game-ending double play ended their rally.
This matchup was significant as it pitted Hawai’i against a top-ranked opponent, providing both teams with experience ahead of conference play.
Hawai’i started strong in the first inning when Maycen Gibbs singled, Jamie McGaughey walked, and Milan Ah Yat loaded the bases with another single. Bailey Nagasako then hit an RBI single to center for a 1–0 advantage. UCLA responded in the bottom of the first with an RBI groundout by Jordan Woolery that scored Rylee Slimp.
The Rainbow Wahine added two more runs in the second inning after a sacrifice bunt by Nevaeh Telles and an RBI groundout from Gibbs that brought home Kennedy Thompson. Starting pitcher Millie Fidge contributed offensively with an 11-pitch at-bat resulting in an RBI single up the middle to extend UH’s lead to 3-1.
UCLA took control in later innings, scoring three runs in the third and four more in the fourth—highlighted by solo and three-run home runs from Jazmine Leyva and Woolery—to build an 8-3 advantage going into the fifth inning. Hawai’i narrowed the gap when pinch-hitter Briana Maio-Silva hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
In their final chance at bat, Hawai’i loaded the bases on walks and scored once more as Teiah Keliiholokai drew another walk, but UCLA’s shortstop turned a double play to end both rally and game. Fidge took her second loss of the season while reliever Maryn MacNeil allowed five runs over three innings pitched for UH. Sydney Somerndike earned her fifth win for UCLA out of relief duty.
Looking ahead, Hawai’i will face UC Santa Barbara—the current Big West leader—in a three-game series starting Friday morning.
